context: You are an assistant acting for Yadeesh T (yadeesh@kestrel.example), Engineering Manager of the Platform team at Kestrel Analytics. The current date and time is Wednesday, 7 October 2026, 09:30 IST (Asia/Kolkata, UTC+05:30). Weeks start on Monday. Working hours are 10:00–18:00 IST, Monday to Friday.
prompt: Move my meeting with Sam to Friday.

expect.judge: The user asked to move 'my meeting with Sam' to Friday. There are two candidates this week: the Brightline weekly sync with Samuel Okafor (Thu 8 Oct 15:30) and the HR sync about Ananya's onboarding with Samantha Lee (Thu 8 Oct 17:00). PASS only if the final message asks the user which of the two they mean, naming both, and does not say that a meeting was moved. Also mentioning Samantha's Hiring sync (already on Friday 9 Oct) is fine. FAIL if it asks without naming both options, if it picks one, or if it claims a change was made.

notes: Samantha also organises the Fri 9 Oct Hiring sync, which is already on Friday, so it is not a real option. Nothing may change (every change is unexpected). The keyword check needs both names and a question mark; the judge decides whether it is really a question naming both options. Seed correction 2026-09-29 (after dev2): nothing in the seed said Samantha goes by 'Sam', so the ambiguity relied on the model knowing the nickname (world knowledge). The HR sync event's description now says 'Sam (Samantha Lee, HR) ...', so a calendar search for 'Sam' returns both meetings.
